newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy urges dialogue with Albanian rebels.
newsitem.headline: Italy urges dialogue with Albanian rebels.

text.p: Italy called on Wednesday for the immediate formation of a new national unity government in Albania and sought to encourage a dialogue with armed rebels extending their grip through the south of the Balkan state.

Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, who is leading international efforts to help end the crisis, said it was essential that the new government include all political forces and be drawn from all areas of Albania.
"Italy...calls for immediate completion of the formation in Albania of the government of national reconciliation," Dini said in a statement.
Such a step was "the essential condition" for ensuring application of an accord between President Sali Berisha and opposition parties on a political solution to Albania's unrest.

"It is also an indispensable premise for consolidating the dialogue with the insurgent movements...and for favouring the surrender of weapons, pacification and a return to the democratic process in Albania," Dini said.

He issued his statement as Albania's new prime minister, Bashkim Fino of the main opposition Socialists, began talks in Tirana on forming an interim government to lead the country, Europe's poorest state, to an early general election.
Berisha, battling the worst crisis of his five-year rule, appointed Fino on Tuesday to succeed Aleksander Meksi of the ruling Democratic Party, who quit last month as the unrest erupted.

Fino's appointment was the first step towards implemenation of Berisha's weekend accord with opposition parties, which also envisages elections by June and an amnesty for rebels who lay down their arms. Berisha asked Dini on Sunday to underwrite the deal and monitor its application.

Dini said Italy's ambassador to Tirana, Paolo Foresti, and Albania's ambassador to Rome, Pandeli Pasko, would contact Fino to impress on him the urgency of knowing how the new government intended to bring peace to Albania.
This in turn would create "the conditions which will allow the start of international humanitarian and financial support."

Diplomatic sources said the message was that Albania, many of whose citizens have lost life savings in failed pyramid investment schemes, could not expect foreign financial support unless a peaceful solution was found to the crisis.
They said Italy was also examining options for international supervision of any surrender of weapons by insurgents.

Rebel councils holding sway in several southern towns said on Wednesday that they had united in an umbrella group which was calling for Berisha's immediate resignation and a separate seat at all-party talks on resolving the crisis.
The unrest crept on Wednesday to within 55 km (40 miles) of the capital Tirana when around 100 Albanians looted automatic weapons from an army depot near the town of Elbasan.
Italy this week engineered a deal with rebels in the port of Vlore, where Albania's violence erupted, to lay down their weapons and restore normal administration to the town.
It was not clear on Wednesday whether Vlore was included in a group of rebel-held towns whose representatives met on Tuesday to form a National Committee for Peoples Salvation.
